headline: SK hynix posted a record quarter and Korea jumped 6.6%, but oil is back near $116 on new Gulf threats and the 10 year is over 5% as the Fed decides at 2pm ET; also, yesterday's XOM and CVX '2R wins' do not pass her volume rule.
summary: The dashboard is still on Oct 26 closes (prices_as_of 2026-10-26), so every close below is the Oct 27 close from Massive, the price source of record. The S&P 500 rose 0.60% to 7,722.60 on Oct 27 as chips led, while Boeing fell 10.7% on 6.7 times normal volume after delaying its 737 ramp (AP, Vantage, Massive). Overnight SK hynix beat on profit and promised about 100 trillion won of shareholder returns; it rose 10.89% and the KOSPI 6.63% (CNBC), and Micron was up 4% premarket (Reuters). Brent rose 1.9% to $116.03 early Wednesday after the Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and the WSJ reported the US told Gulf states to expect a short, intense campaign against Iran after the Nov 3 midterms (Dow Jones via Morningstar, OilPrice). The Fed is expected to hold at 3.75% to 4.00% today, with a December hike nearly priced (CNBC, LSEG). Correction: the XOM and CVX swings never closed over their entries on 1.5 times normal volume, and CVX reached its target only intraday, so yesterday's '2R win' calls do not hold by her rule.

regime.why: AI money is still flowing (SK hynix's record quarter, chips up two days in a row), but the 10 year is back above 5% and oil rebuilt its war premium overnight. The Fed is expected to pause today and hike in December, and the main tail risk is a renewed US campaign against Iran after the midterms.

signals.title: SK hynix's record quarter lifted Korea 6.6% and Micron premarket; it also locked in more than half of 2027 and 2028 output
signals.since_yesterday: The results are out: revenue 104.6 trillion won and operating profit 83.3 trillion won, both above estimates, plus about 100 trillion won of shareholder returns.
signals.what_happened: SK hynix reported Q3 revenue of 104.62 trillion won (about $78.9 billion), up 327.9% from a year ago, against 98.34 trillion expected, and operating profit of 83.33 trillion won against 76.72 trillion expected, an 80% margin (CNBC, company release). It plans about 100 trillion won of shareholder returns, including at least 30 trillion won of dividends and 60 trillion won of buybacks and cancellations, and it dropped the Solidigm IPO for now. It said 14 major customers signed long term deals covering more than 50% of its 2027 and 2028 capacity, that DRAM prices rose by a high 20s percentage from Q2, and that HBM4 should pass HBM3E in shipments and revenue in Q4 (CNBC). The shares closed up 10.89% in Seoul and the KOSPI 6.63% (CNBC). Before the US open, the SK hynix ADR (SKHY) was up 7.8% and Micron 4% (Reuters, 5:38am ET). On Oct 27, AMD closed at 560.26, up 5.45% on 1.03 times its 50 day volume, and MU at 928.76, up 2.77% (Massive). In the Anthropic story, the new facts are a letter from Sen. Elizabeth Warren demanding answers on risks named in the filing (WSJ via Morningstar) and a report that two customers made up about 20% of first half revenue (Barchart); the WSJ says most of the $80.7 billion first half loss is an accounting adjustment tied to financing.
signals.so_what: Follow the money: when buyers commit to two years of memory output in advance, memory stops being a commodity and becomes the chokepoint. That lets SK hynix pay out about 100 trillion won while still raising investment, and it makes HBM supply, not GPU supply, the limit on AI servers through 2027. Second order: the buyers are the same cloud companies reporting tonight, so their capex guidance either confirms or questions those contracts. Third order: Susquehanna still prefers Micron and Samsung on risk and reward (CNBC), so a rising tide may lift the US name, MU, the most for US accounts. What would make this wrong: Microsoft or Alphabet cutting capex plans, or memory prices peaking as new capacity arrives in 2027.
signals.for_you: Swing: no chip entries before Microsoft and Alphabet report tonight. AMD's 5.45% jump came on only 1.03 times normal volume, so it is not a confirmed breakout, and it now sits about 0.2% above the top of its 468.95 to 558.90 zone (my calculation; Oct 26 zone). ARK sold AMD for a second day (see Inbox). MU has 'Not enough data' on the dashboard. Puts: none. Long term: no change; NVDA and AMD stay 'Buy zone, wait for the chart'.

signals.title: Fed day: a hold is priced, but the 10 year is back over 5% and a December hike is nearly certain in futures
signals.since_yesterday: The 10 year rose back above 5% this morning, and Goldman says the Fed is now hiking every other meeting.
signals.what_happened: The Fed decides at 2pm ET with Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 2:30pm ET. CME FedWatch puts the chance of a hike today under 10%, which would leave the rate at 3.75% to 4.00% after September's quarter point hike (CNBC). LSEG data show a 91% chance of no change today and a December hike almost fully priced (Dow Jones via Morningstar), and traders see at least three more quarter point hikes by late 2027 (Reuters). Cleveland's Hammack, Dallas's Logan and Minneapolis's Kashkari could dissent in favor of a hike (CNBC). JPMorgan's Michael Feroli notes the Fed hiked in September after a 0.2% core PCE print and may hold now with a 0.3% print expected for September (CNBC). The 10 year yield rose 1.8 basis points to 5.010% early Wednesday (Tradeweb via Dow Jones). Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close; September PCE and Q3 GDP, expected at 3.2%, come Thursday (Reuters).
signals.so_what: A hold with a hawkish tone is the base case, so the market reaction depends on Warsh's words and tonight's cloud numbers more than on the decision. Rates above 5% raise the bar for every long duration story, which is why the market keeps asking whether AI spending pays off. Second order: higher rates make cash secured put premium richer, but they also make heavily indebted and long dated growth names fall harder on bad news. What would make this wrong: a surprise hike today, or a soft PCE print Thursday that pushes the December hike out.
signals.for_you: Swing: no new entries before 2pm ET, and none in MSFT or GOOGL before tonight's reports. Puts: wait for the Fed and the VIX to settle; Setups has no put candidates on Oct 26 closes. Long term: no change. Note the 10 year at 5.01% is now the bar any put premium must beat on an annual basis.

signals.title: Oil rebuilt its war premium: a claimed strike on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery and a report of US plans for Iran after the midterms
signals.since_yesterday: Brent fell 1.7% to $113.88 on Oct 27, then rose 1.9% to $116.03 early Wednesday on new Houthi claims and a WSJ report about a post election US campaign.
signals.what_happened: December Brent settled down 1.7% at $113.88 on Oct 27 as talks with Iran continued (WSJ). Early Wednesday it rose 1.9% to $116.03 and WTI 2% to $101.91 (Dow Jones via Morningstar). Yemen's Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on the 550,000 barrel a day Ras Tanura refinery; details are disputed, while Saudi officials reported intercepting other attacks (OilPrice). The WSJ reported that the US told several Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign against Iran after the Nov 3 midterms (Dow Jones via Morningstar). CNBC reports the war's cost at about $47 billion, with President Trump saying it will end 'when I want it to'. On Oct 27 the big US refiners fell hard: Valero 9.24%, Marathon Petroleum 7.36% and Phillips 66 7.03% (Investing.com); I could not confirm why.
signals.so_what: Yesterday the market traded the talks; today it is pricing a second round of war. A plan that is reported a week before a vote may be leverage, not a decision, so headlines can swing both ways. Who pays: airlines, chemicals and anyone with diesel costs, plus Europe and India, which import most of their oil (the rupee closed at 95.23 per dollar, Moneycontrol). Who gets paid: producers with barrels outside the Gulf and US LNG exporters. What would make this wrong: a deal that reopens Hormuz, which would pull oil down fast, as in 1990 (see the cycle card).
signals.for_you: Swing: no new energy swings with XOM and CVX reporting Oct 30 and a war headline risk either way; see the correction signal on their plans. COP (147.96, stop 135.75) and EOG (161.10, stop 147.98) stay open, both on light volume (0.88 and 0.77 times normal, Massive, Oct 27). DAL closed at 81.45, up 2.89% on 1.01 times normal volume, so it is not ready; higher oil is a headwind. No put ideas.

signals.title: Correction: the XOM and CVX '2R wins' do not pass her volume rule, and CVX only touched its target intraday
signals.since_yesterday: Rechecked on Massive daily bars: neither entry was ever confirmed by a close over the pivot on 1.5 times the 50 day volume.
signals.what_happened: Yesterday's brief and the scorecard closed both swings as 2R wins on Oct 26. Massive daily bars say otherwise. XOM (entry 169.99, stop 162.99, target 183.99): the scorecard marked it triggered on Oct 9, but that day it only touched 170.29 intraday and closed at 168.94 on 0.58 times its 50 day volume. Its first close over the entry was Oct 12 at 172.15 on 0.64 times. From Oct 5 to Oct 27 its heaviest day was 1.07 times (Oct 27), so it never had a 1.5 times close over the pivot. It did close at 184.54 on Oct 26, above the 183.99 target. CVX (entry 218.23, stop 210.45, target 233.79): the Oct 13 'trigger' was an intraday touch of 218.79 with a 217.73 close on 0.87 times; its first close over the entry was Oct 14 at 222.04 on 1.11 times, and no day reached 1.5 times. Its best close was 233.21 on Oct 23; the 234.08 high on Oct 26 was intraday only, and it closed at 232.01. On Oct 27 XOM closed at 179.91 and CVX at 228.23 (Massive), about 1.42R and 1.29R above entry (my calculation).
signals.so_what: By her rule these were never confirmed breakouts, so they should be scored as 'not triggered', not as wins. The price idea worked, but the volume rule exists so the scorecard measures her actual method; counting intraday touches inflates the hit rate. The scorecard code marks a trigger on any intraday high over the entry and a win on any intraday high over the target, with no volume check. That should be fixed and tested before Saturday's scorecard.
signals.for_you: Swing: if you took these trades anyway, they are open trades, not finished wins: XOM is about 1.42R up and CVX about 1.29R up on Oct 27 closes. Both report Oct 30, so the plan rule says take profits or tighten stops before the reports rather than hold through them. Treat the scorecard's swing hit rate as overstated until the grading follows the close and volume rule.

signals.title: Boeing fell 10.7% on 6.7 times normal volume after pushing its 737 ramp into 2027
signals.since_yesterday: The stock reaction and the reason: the 737 delay and a weak cash outlook, not the revenue beat yesterday's brief noted.
signals.what_happened: Boeing posted a core loss of $0.34 a share against $0.21 expected on revenue of $24.19 billion, and said 737 output will stabilize at 47 a month only in early 2027, with the step to 52 in the second half (Vantage citing CNBC and Reuters). Jefferies says Boeing expects about $3 billion of free cash flow next year against a $5.5 billion consensus (Reuters via Spokesman-Review). The stock fell $20.13 to 168.18, a 52 week low (Vantage), on 47.3 million shares, 6.73 times its 50 day average (Massive). Yesterday's brief quoted a 26 cent loss from TheStreet; CNBC and Reuters give the core loss as 34 cents.
signals.so_what: Heavy volume on a big down day is distribution: funds are leaving, and that rarely ends in one session. The cash shortfall matters most, because Boeing's suppliers are paid from it. Second order: slower 737 output delays deliveries to airlines that need new, fuel efficient planes as oil sits above $100, and it keeps the plane market tight for Airbus. What would make this wrong: a quick fix to the supplier and quality issues that brings the ramp back into 2026.
signals.for_you: No action. BA is 'Avoid' on the dashboard and far above its fair value zone. Do not sell puts on a falling name with a cash shortfall, however rich the premium looks.

The real recovering faster than stocks says the currency panic eased, while the banks wait for the rate decision. Banks are the weak link: a Selic hike raises funding costs and loan losses at the same time, which is the risk Citi just flagged. What would make this wrong: a credible spending plan from Lula's team before Nov 3.

signals.title: Bausch + Lomb beat and raised; GE Vernova's backlog reached $197 billion as gas turbine orders more than doubled
signals.what_happened: Bausch + Lomb reported Q3 revenue of $1.38 billion, up 7.3%, adjusted EPS of $0.34 against $0.22 expected, and raised its 2026 revenue outlook to about $5.50 billion at the midpoint; surgical revenue rose to $234 million from $215 million and operating cash flow to $233 million from $137 million (company release via Morningstar, StockStory via TradingView). StockStory had the stock up 3.3% after the release. Boston Scientific posted adjusted EPS of $0.73, $0.02 short of estimates, on revenue of $5.14 billion, up 1.5%, and the stock slid (Investing.com). GE Vernova reported orders of $29.3 billion, up 96% organically, Power orders up 178%, a $197 billion backlog, gas turbine backlog plus reservations of 122 GW heading to at least 130 GW by year end, and a raised 2026 outlook (company release).
signals.so_what: For eye care, Bausch + Lomb's surgical and cash flow gains show the turnaround is working; cash flow matters because the company still carries heavy debt. For power, GE Vernova's 16.6 GW of gas turbine orders in one quarter (10-Q via StockTitan) says data centers are locking in gas plants years ahead, which makes turbine slots, not chips, the bottleneck for new AI capacity. Boston Scientific's slowdown to 1.5% growth is a warning for medtech names priced for double digit growth.
signals.for_you: Long term: BLCO was 'Buy zone now' at 17.58 on Oct 26, near the top of its 16.13 to 17.67 zone; a 3.3% pop would put it above the zone, so wait for a pullback into the zone rather than chase. GEV is on the AI power map; no rating change today. No swings or puts.

headwinds: Oil near $116 with war risk rising after the midterms.
A 10 year yield above 5% and a Fed still hiking.

history.when: July to October 1990, Iraq's invasion of Kuwait
history.what: Oil prices doubled from July to October 1990, then fell nearly back to where they started within months, once the outcome of the war was clear.
history.lesson: War premiums in oil can vanish fast. Producers bought near the peak of fear give back gains quickly when the threat resolves, so take swing profits by plan rather than holding for more fear.

source.title: Are there useful lessons from the 1990-91 oil price shock? (The Energy Journal via JSTOR)

history.when: 1999 to March 2000, the dot com IPO wave
history.what: 476 US companies went public in 1999, raising $36.94 billion with an average first day gain of 71% (Ritter). The Nasdaq peaked in March 2000, shortly after the issuance peak.
history.lesson: When companies rush to sell stock, they are telling you prices are high. Today's AI firms have real revenue, but two customers making up about 20% of Anthropic's first half revenue is the kind of concentration to watch.

source.title: IPO statistics: 1999 count, proceeds and first day returns (Jay Ritter, University of Florida)

cycle.differences: In 1990 the Fed was cutting into a recession; today it is hiking with growth still near 3%, so an oil spike now pushes rates up rather than down. Unlike 1999, the AI sellers have fast growing sales and contracted demand, but rates are far higher.
cycle.for_you: Swing: nothing new before the Fed and big tech tonight; treat XOM and CVX as open trades to manage into Oct 30, not wins. Puts: none; the 10 year at 5.01% is the bar any premium must beat. Long term: only 'Buy zone now' names that are not reporting this week, and do not chase BLCO above its zone.

principle.text: Pain plus reflection equals progress (paraphrased from Principles).
principle.applied: Finding that two 'wins' did not follow the volume rule is a small pain. Fixing how the scorecard grades trades turns it into a better system, which is worth more than two flattering results.
